entry.title: Released API DDLS Was Deleted ATC Error in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Despite Object No Longer
entry.content:
Hello,

I am working in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and I am facing compatibility ATC errors during ATC checks.

The following ATC errors are raised:

  • Released API DDLS ZDD_SD_TEST was deleted

  • Released API DDLS ZDD_SD_OPENORDERITEM was deleted

  • Released API DDLS ZDD_SD_DELIVERY was deleted

Error example:

Changes in ZSD (DEVC), compared to version 100 (CG4), found by component BC-SRV-APS-EXT-REL:
Released API DDLS ZDD_SD_TEST was deleted.

Background:

  • These CDS views were previously released as APIs (C1 contract).

  • The CDS views no longer exist in the system.

  • When searching in ADT (Ctrl+Shift+A), the objects cannot be found.

  • In the "Manage API Snapshots" application, I cannot find these CDS views in the current SAP Default snapshot.

  • However, the compatibility ATC check still reports them as deleted APIs.

I found SAP KBA 3442779 which explains that released APIs may remain in historical API snapshots and can continue to trigger compatibility checks even after deletion.

My questions are:

  1. How can I identify the exact snapshot that still contains these deleted CDS views?

  2. If the objects no longer exist and were never delivered to customers, what is the recommended way to remove these compatibility findings?

  3. Is setting the default snapshot to "Not Check Relevant" the only solution, or is there another recommended approach?

  4. Has anyone experienced a similar issue with deleted released CDS views in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?

Any guidance would be appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: Warehouse Task Concept in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – Mapping from SAP Business ByDesign Inte
entry.content:
We are currently working with a customer who uses a .NET-based solution integrated with SAP Business ByDesign.

In the current ByD setup, warehouse operators work based on logistics tasks generated by the system (e.g., Goods Receipt, Stock Transfer, Picking). Our WMS consumes these tasks and allows operators to execute and confirm them. This process is supported through APIs such as SiteLogisticsTask and WarehouseConfirmation.

 

The customer is now evaluating a transition to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and would like to maintain the same operational model.

 

While we understand that S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition provides Warehouse Management capabilities and supports API-based integration with external systems, we are struggling to identify the equivalent of the ByD logistics task concept.

 

Our questions are:

  • Is there an equivalent to ByD Logistics Tasks / Warehouse Tasks in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?
  • Can these tasks be created, retrieved, processed, and confirmed through standard APIs by an external WMS?
  • Which business objects and APIs should be considered as the equivalent of SiteLogisticsTask and WarehouseConfirmation in ByD?
  • Are there any limitations or recommended approaches when implementing a task-driven warehouse execution process with an external WMS in Public Cloud?

Our objective is to offer the customer the same warehouse execution experience they currently have in ByD while following SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition best practices and Clean Core principles.

Any guidance, architecture recommendations, or references to relevant APIs and business objects would be greatly appreciated.

entry.title: Can SAP API Management directly invoke SAP S/4HANA OData services without SAP Cloud Integration?
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I have an architectural question regarding the use of SAP API Management and would appreciate your insights.

Scenario

I have a client application that sends data to an API Proxy in SAP API Management. Instead of forwarding the request to an SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) iFlow, I am considering calling an SAP S/4HANA OData service directly from the API Proxy.

Since the target OData service requires an X-CSRF token for POST operations, the API Proxy would need to perform the following steps:

  1. Receive the incoming request from the client.
  2. Fetch the X-CSRF token from the SAP S/4HANA OData service.
  3. Reuse the token (and cookies, if required) to execute the POST request.
  4. Return the response back to the client.

My Questions

  1. Is this architecture technically feasible using only SAP API Management, without involving SAP Cloud Integration (CPI)?
  2. Can SAP API Management reliably handle the complete X-CSRF token flow (token retrieval, cookie handling, and POST request)?
  3. Is this approach recommended for production environments, or are there any technical limitations or best practices that should be considered?
  4. What would be the major drawbacks compared to using SAP Cloud Integration, particularly regarding:
    • Error handling
    • Retry mechanisms
    • Monitoring and logging
    • Security
    • Scalability
    • Maintainability

Why I'm Asking

The motivation behind this approach is to optimize SAP Cloud Integration message consumption and potentially reduce licensing costs for simple pass-through scenarios. If API Management can securely and reliably handle such integrations, it could eliminate the need for an iFlow in certain use cases.

Has anyone implemented a similar architecture in a production environment? If so, I would appreciate hearing about your experience and whether you would recommend this approach.

Thank you in advance for your guidance!

entry.title: Correlation of Different HTTP Methods in SAP Cloud ALM to ServiceNow Integration
entry.content:
We have integrated SAP Cloud ALM (CALM) with ServiceNow and have evaluated both the Table API and the Scripted API approaches.
Our requirement is to support the following operations:

POST – Create a new event/ticket in ServiceNow.
GET – Retrieve existing ticket details and correlation information.
PATCH – Update an existing ServiceNow ticket.

Current Challenge
When using the Scripted API, we are only able to configure and invoke a single HTTP method. As a result, we are unable to understand how multiple operations (POST, GET, and PATCH) can be handled within the same integration scenario.
For example:

When a Cloud ALM event is created, we need to perform a POST to create a ServiceNow ticket.
After the ticket is created, we need a GET to retrieve or validate the ServiceNow record and correlation details.
For subsequent incident updates, we need to perform a PATCH against the existing ServiceNow ticket.

However, in the Scripted API configuration, it appears that only one method call can be defined, which makes it unclear how create and update scenarios should be handled within the same integration flow.
Questions

  • How can SAP Cloud ALM invoke different HTTP methods (POST, GET, and PATCH) when using the Scripted API?
  • Is there a mechanism within Scripted API to dynamically switch the HTTP method based on the business scenario (create vs. update)?
  • How is the correlation between SAP Cloud ALM incidents and ServiceNow tickets maintained when different methods are required?

entry.title: SAP Cloud Integration - Questions
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

Our client has requested us to answer the following questions before even implementing the interface... Could you please help us to get the answers for the following questions? Should we Implement Pipeline concept to acheive some of the functionalities?

We have two interfaces (i) Synchronous Inbound Interface and (ii) Asynchronous Inbound Interface that should be implemented on SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration)….

Asynch : Sender ---> SAP Integration Suite(Cloud Integration) --> SAP S4/HANA

Synch : Sender <---> SAP Integration Suite(API Management + Cloud Integration) <--> SAP S4/HANA


1. Endpoint and communication details

2. XML Validation : Must the XML be validated against the XSD on the sender side?

3. Character encoding and special characters : How are special characters handled?

4. Error catalogue

(i) Technical Errors (ii) Business Errors (iii) Security errors

5. Retry handling : Is automatic retry performed?

6. Error feedback to the Sender : (i) What information does the sender receive? Are error codes available?
(ii) Are standardized error messages available? (iii) In which language are errors returned?

7. Monitoring and consistency controls : How is it detected that data is no longer being sent or received?
How are erroneous messages detected?

8. Alerting : Which events trigger an alert in CALM? Who receives alerts?

9. Logging, storage and audit Trail : Is every incoming message stored? Is every outgoing message stored? Are changes logged?

10.Authentication and encryption : How does the sender authenticate? Are technical users used? Are certificates used? How is message integrity ensured? Are messages digitally signed? Are transmissions encrypted?

Regards

Ramu

entry.title: API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV sandbox returns 401 - gateway/backend auth mismatch
entry.content:
I'm getting a consistent 401 Unauthorized calling the API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV sandbox API (A_MatlStkInAcctMod entity), and I've isolated it to something on the sandbox backend, not my credentials.

Request:

 
GET /s4hanacloud/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV/A_MatlStkInAcctMod?$filter=Material eq 'CH_C_104'&$format=json
Header: APIKey: <my key>

Response: 401 Nicht autorisiert (SAP's own HTML error page)

Response headers include:

 
www-authenticate: Basic realm="SAP NetWeaver Application Server [EJS/100][alias]"
sap-authenticated: false
sap-system: EJS

This suggests the public API gateway is accepting the request, but the backend NetWeaver system it forwards to is expecting HTTP Basic Auth instead of the API key — a gateway-to-backend mismatch, not an invalid key.

What I've already ruled out:

  • Confirmed the API key is current via "Show API Key" in account settings
  • Regenerated a fresh API key — same result
  • Tested via curl directly and via the API's own "Try Out" tool on this page — same 401 both ways
  • API status on its overview page shows "Active," not deprecated

Timing: the issue started around when the API's page showed "Last Modified: 10 Sep 2026, Version 1.1.0" — possibly related to that update. It's now been several days with no change.

Has anyone else hit this, or is there a known issue with this sandbox after the recent version update? Happy to share my API key ID or further details if useful for troubleshooting.

Update: I tested a sibling entity in the same API product, A_MaterialSerialNumber, and it returns 200 successfully through the same key and the same "Try Out" tool. Only A_MatlStkInAcctMod specifically returns 401. This confirms it's isolated to this one entity's backend, not the API product, key, or subscription as a whole

entry.title: SAP API Management - Unable to rewrite backend target URL/path dynamically
entry.content:
I am facing an issue in SAP Integration Suite - API Management regarding backend URL rewriting before the request is sent to the target endpoint.

My public endpoint:

GET /gestaopessoas/funcionarios/cpf?matricula=10071015

Backend that should be called:

https://<host>/http/ura/cpfconsultation?matricula=10071015

Instead, SAP APIM always calls:

https://<host>/http/funcionarios/cpf?matricula=10071015

My Environment

  • SAP Integration Suite
  • SAP API Management
  • API Proxy created manually (not generated from OpenAPI)
  • Target Endpoint type: URL (not API Provider)
  • OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials implemented successfully using:
    • KVM
    • BasicAuthentication
    • ServiceCallout
    • ExtractVariables
    • AssignMessage

The OAuth flow is working correctly.

The only remaining issue is rewriting the backend URL/path.

What we already tested

We tested several approaches.

JavaScript

We successfully executed JavaScript inside the ProxyEndpoint Flow.

We changed:

context.setVariable("target.url", "...");

context.setVariable("request.path", "...");

context.setVariable("dynamic.target", "...");

context.setVariable("target.copy.pathsuffix", false);

The Trace confirms that all variables are correctly updated.

Example:

dynamic.target =
https://<host>/http/ura/cpfconsultation?matricula=10071015

and

target.copy.pathsuffix = false

However, in the final execution step SAP API Management ignores all these values.

The final Trace always shows:

target.url =
https://<host>/http

request.uri =
/http/funcionarios/cpf

request.path =
/http/funcionarios/cpf

which means the runtime rebuilds the backend URL before sending the request.

AssignMessage

We also tried using AssignMessage to modify:

  • Path
  • request.path
  • target.url

However either:

  • the policy XML is rejected by the parser, or
  • the runtime ignores the modifications.

ServiceCallout

ServiceCallout is working correctly.

It successfully obtains an OAuth token from the OAuth Authorization Server.

Therefore the issue is unrelated to OAuth.

Expected behavior

We expect SAP API Management to allow rewriting the backend URI before sending the request.

For example:

Public URI

/funcionarios/cpf

should become

/ura/cpfconsultation

without changing the public API exposed to consumers.
In my opinion this is a common API Gateway feature.

Question
Could you please clarify:

  1. Is backend path rewriting supported in SAP API Management?
  2. Is there any supported policy or configuration to rewrite the backend URI before sending the request?
  3. Is modifying target.url, request.path, dynamic.target or target.copy.pathsuffix supported?
  4. Is this behavior expected when using URL Target Endpoints?
  5. If backend URI rewriting is supported, could you provide the recommended approach?

From what I saw it appears that MCP gateway is not responding correctly for enabling Protected Resource Metadata Discovery . I am no expert in this. What I saw (experiment in the picture below) was that authorization_servers (rfc9728, section 2) is token endpoint. My reading is that it should be Authorization Server Metadata rfc8414, 3.2 or OpenID Discovery Configuration. So, in case of XSUAA it should be /.well-known/openid-configuration.
